source: MorphWiki quantum rewrite transition sparse attention

rules.rule: The rewrite converts a noun-indexed encyclopedia into a derivation graph.
rules.new_information: The new object is not a better summary of each topic; it is an ordering relation: which topic plays context, state, generator, observable, readout, compatibility, boundary, field, protocol, or annotation.

rules.rule: The dominant stable role is operator-to-spectrum readout, not object naming.
rules.new_information: The rewrite makes explicit that many named quantum topics become different ways of asking a legal spectral question of a state.

rules.rule: Particles become stable role-realizations inside field/mode/readout machinery.
rules.new_information: The particle pages are not discarded; they are relocated as field/mode/statistics/readout constructions. This is a more precise statement than 'particles are not fundamental'.

rules.rule: Interpretations mostly act on state, probability, and update semantics.
rules.new_information: QBism, relational quantum mechanics, collapse language, and popular frames can be kept without letting them become false roots of the derivation tree.

rules.rule: Boundary pages are realization gates: they change allowed spectra without changing the core prediction problem.
rules.new_information: Tunnelling, particle-in-a-box, scattering, cavities, and spectral lines become one family: boundary-shaped spectra.

rules.rule: Protocol pages compose state preparation, maps, and readouts.
rules.new_information: Quantum computing is reorganized as controlled composition of states, operators, readouts, and error constraints rather than a separate ontology of qubits.

rules.rule: Anomalies identify where several formal roles coincide.

top_anomalies.title: Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen paradox
top_anomalies.explanation: EPR is a compatibility test. The mechanism is a bipartite state, separated measurement contexts, and a correlation readout that cannot be reduced to pre-existing local values. The formal starting point is the joint state and local observables; the question is which correlation constraint fails.

top_anomalies.title: Quantum biology
top_anomalies.explanation: Quantum biology is an open-system transfer problem. The environment is part of the boundary that may preserve, destroy, or select coherence. The formal fields are the state carrier, environmental coupling, coherence or transport observable, and classical control.

top_anomalies.title: Measurement problem
top_anomalies.explanation: The measurement problem is a readout junction. It sits where unitary state transport, detector context, probability assignment, and state update meet. The formal decomposition is pre-measurement evolution, apparatus or environment coupling, POVM or projection readout, and post-record conditioning.

top_anomalies.title: Quantum gravity
top_anomalies.explanation: Quantum gravity is a field/boundary junction. It asks whether geometry becomes part of the quantum state carrier or remains a realization layer for an operator theory. The missing formal objects are a state of geometry, a constraint or evolution operator, a boundary or semiclassical readout, and a test of which geometric quantities survive quantization.

top_anomalies.title: Scattering
top_anomalies.explanation: Scattering is a boundary-to-spectrum mechanism. The central map is from asymptotic in-states to out-states. The relevant objects are the interaction region, asymptotic channels, S-matrix or cross-section readout, and conservation constraints.

top_anomalies.title: Schrödinger's cat
top_anomalies.explanation: Schrödinger's cat is a macroscopic readout protocol. It couples microscopic unitary evolution to a macroscopic boundary and forces three steps apart: coherent transport, decoherence or apparatus coupling, and the rule by which one record is selected or conditioned.

top_anomalies.title: Wave–particle duality
top_anomalies.explanation: Wave-particle duality is a representation/readout switch. The same carrier is interrogated through incompatible experimental contexts, so the observed pattern changes from interference-like to count-like. Its compact form is context selection plus readout channel.

top_anomalies.title: Quantum state
top_anomalies.explanation: Quantum state is the carrier rather than the final prediction. It precedes admissibility, evolution, observable choice, and probability readout. The unresolved distinction is whether the carrier is a vector, density operator, field state, or register, and which transformations preserve it.

rules.new_information: EPR, the measurement problem, quantum gravity, quantum biology, and related pages combine several formal questions in one topic: state preparation, compatibility, boundary or environmental coupling, protocol order, and readout.

top_transition_pages.title: Macroscopic quantum phenomena
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: This state page mixes state evolution, preparation and boundary context, and normalization and admissibility. The relevant fields are the state carrier, representation, evolution, admissibility, and later readout.

top_transition_pages.title: Bell's theorem
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: This measurement page mixes observables and spectra, state evolution, and normalization and admissibility. Separate the state before readout, the detector or measurement map, the recorded outcome, and the update or conditioning rule.

top_transition_pages.title: Quantum simulator
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: A quantum simulator is an engineered realization of another Hamiltonian or channel. It is both an observable system and a protocol for representing a target system. The formal fields are the simulated target, physical carrier, encoding map, and validation observable.

top_transition_pages.title: Delayed-choice quantum eraser
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: The delayed-choice eraser is a protocol-order stress test. Its mechanism is the arrangement of which-path information, later measurement choice, and conditional correlation readout. The relevant statistics are defined only after the full measurement protocol is specified.

top_transition_pages.title: Quantum field theory
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: This field-level page mixes observables and spectra, state evolution, and normalization and admissibility. Treat it as a many-mode or geometric realization problem: identify the state sector or field algebra, then the constraints and readout that make the field content observable.

top_transition_pages.title: Quantum nonlocality
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: This measurement page mixes observables and spectra, state evolution, and controlled update protocol. Separate the state before readout, the detector or measurement map, the recorded outcome, and the update or conditioning rule.

top_transition_pages.title: Wave function
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: The wave function is a representation of the state carrier. It stores amplitude, phase, normalization, basis choice, and probability potential in one object. The formal decomposition separates representation, admissibility, evolution, and Born readout.

top_transition_pages.title: Wave–particle duality

top_transition_pages.title: Spin (physics)
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: This state page mixes observables and spectra, state evolution, and normalization and admissibility. The relevant fields are the state carrier, representation, evolution, admissibility, and later readout.

top_transition_pages.title: Quantum cellular automaton
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: A quantum cellular automaton is a locality-preserving update rule. The lattice, neighborhood rule, unitarity or channel condition, and update protocol define the mechanism together.

top_transition_pages.title: Quantum electrodynamics
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: Quantum electrodynamics is a field-interaction construction. It combines gauge admissibility, charged matter states, photon modes, perturbative transport, and scattering/readout. The relevant formal objects are field operators, gauge constraints, interaction terms, and observable amplitudes.

top_transition_pages.title: Fermi–Dirac statistics
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: Fermi-Dirac statistics is an admissibility rule for many-particle states. The mechanism is antisymmetry and occupation restriction. The formal content is anticommutation, exclusion, occupation numbers, and the thermodynamic readout derived from that constrained state space.

top_transition_pages.title: Schrödinger picture
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: This page sits between Dynamics and transformations and Quantum states and subsystem structure. The ambiguity is useful: it marks a place where two formal roles meet and require separate treatment before the page supports a derivation.

top_transition_pages.title: Hamiltonian (quantum mechanics)
top_transition_pages.anomaly_explanation: The Hamiltonian has two roles: it generates time evolution and, as an observable, supplies an energy spectrum. The formal split is domain/self-adjointness, unitary transport, conserved energy, and spectral readout.

uses.name: Derivation order
uses.why_useful: The domain or Hilbert space precedes the state; the state precedes the generator or measurement map; the spectrum and probability rule precede interpretation. This order keeps particles, protocols, and interpretations downstream of the formal construction they use.
uses.evidence_needed: A page needs local equations or a clear route placement showing which formal role is being used.

uses.name: Pages that need explicit equations
uses.why_useful: The 42 topic-specific pages already supply local equation skeletons. The 104 core-derived pages mark topics where the book can state the expected quantum ingredients, but still needs a page-native state, operator or map, spectrum or readout, compatibility condition, and realization.
uses.evidence_needed: Clean equation witnesses and page-local role rows linked to the source text.

uses.name: Role-based topic comparison
uses.why_useful: Two topics can be compared when they preserve the same state-operator-readout pattern, even if their historical names differ. A valid comparison should keep track of the Hilbert space or domain, operator class, spectrum, probability rule, and compatibility condition.
uses.evidence_needed: Route profiles, equation witnesses, and a check that the compared topics share the relevant formal roles.

uses.name: Mixed-role topics
uses.why_useful: Pages such as EPR, the measurement problem, quantum gravity, and quantum biology combine compatibility, boundary, protocol, and transport roles. They require decomposition into separate formal questions before they can be presented as derivations.
uses.evidence_needed: Targeted source-equation checks for each role claimed on the page.

uses.name: Interpretation layer
uses.why_useful: Interpretive pages change the status assigned to state vectors, probabilities, updates, observers, or recorded outcomes. They do not by themselves replace the Hamiltonian, operator algebra, spectral decomposition, or Born-rule assignment.
uses.evidence_needed: Explicit separation between formal equations and claims about state, probability, update, or ontology.

practical_conclusion: The transition map separates pages with local equation support from pages that still require local equations. It also identifies mixed-role pages and role-preserving comparisons across topics. The new information is structural: the topic encyclopedia becomes an ordered set of formal questions and unresolved derivations.
